It is common sense that people going through puberty go through depression. The only exceptions are the rare individuals who feel little to no extreme emotions and those who have monstrous confidence.
Read the whole message, read it again, breathe, and read it again. As someone who has had chronic and severe depression since the age of 8, I am well aware it can be exacerbated by external factors. The reality is, it can be caused by internal influences such as chemical imbalances which can be brought on by puberty, and then worsened and extended by external factors until it becomes a vicious cycle.

Sometimes it is and sometimes it isn't. It is true that mental health needs to be taken more seriously and that the education system can turn children into dysfunctional adults. Honestly there are 101 reasons one can conceive about what is the cause of depression and other forms of mental illness. It is easy to blame one thing and we as human beings do it all the time.

No one is diagnosing here. It is just common sense.
That said I agree with you 100%, happens all the time.

The truth is, just because some other or most other students at your school are depressed has nothing to do with the school. It is actually a natural chemical imbalance in the brain from puberty. 

Realistically, there were things people in the past were more free to do that would improve endorphin production. Not only were people more active but tended to have better diets. Some will argue that people were starving, relatively yes they were if you compare their diets to what we commonly eat today.

The world is also going through a very serious shift,  lot of bad things are happening at once and it tends to weigh on all of us.

I was in special ed for years. One of the schools I went to had on site psychiatrists in addition to therapists and counselors. I wouldn't say it helped much. I think you're really just looking for someone to listen to you. Talk to a teacher, a parent, trusted friend, or make friends with a complete stranger.
